deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: The Dots3 NOTE model itself is CUDA-only and needs no NPU adaptation. The real impact is the shared change in vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py::MLACommonMetadataBuilder.__init__ (parent of AscendMLAMetadataBuilder/AscendSFAMetadataBuilder/AscendMlaDCPMetadataBuilder/AscendDSAMetadataBuilder): it now reads MLA dims from `compilation_config.static_forward_context[layer_names[0]]` (requiring layer attributes q_lora_rank, kv_lora_rank, qk_nope_head_dim, qk_rope_head_dim, v_head_dim) instead of `get_mla_dims(model_config)`, and sizes `chunked_prefill_workspace` as `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` instead of `model_config.get_head_size()`. Adaptation steps: (1) Audit every attention layer that can become `layer_names[0]` of an MLA/SFA/DSA KV-cache group to confirm it is registered in static_forward_context and carries those 5 attributes - verified OK for AscendMultiHeadLatentAttention (ops/mla.py), vLLM MLAAttention (registered at '{prefix}.attn'), DeepseekV4 MLA, and models/layer/attention/layer.py; (2) confirm the workspace width change is a no-op for standard MLA models (head_size == kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim) - it is, and it is actually more correct for hybrid per-layer-dims models like DeepSeek V4 which ascend already supports via AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec; (3) add unit-test coverage for the real (un-mocked) parent __init__ path in tests/ut/attention/a2/test_mla_v1.py and test_sfa_v1.py, since they currently mock MLACommonMetadataBuilder.__init__; (4) review patch/platform/patch_speculative_config.py (which wholesale-replaces SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override) to confirm the new upstream dots3_note branch is not silently dropped - harmless for NPU but worth a comment, and ensure the new 'dots3_note_mtp' member of MTPModelTypes does not break patch_pp_mtp.py's set(get_args(MTPModelTypes)) logic (it does not). No changes needed to MLAAttention usage: the new optional sliding_window/prefill_backend_cls kwargs are backward compatible and ascend builds its own AscendMLAAttentionSpec/AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec.
deep_analysis.risk: Low. The main hazard is the new hard dependency of MLACommonMetadataBuilder.__init__ on `static_forward_context[layer_names[0]]` existing and exposing the 5 MLA-dim attributes; if any ascend MLA/SFA/DSA layer is ever registered in a KV group without them (e.g. a future CacheOnlyAttentionLayer or a plain Indexer landing in the same group), builder construction raises AttributeError/KeyError at model-load time on NPU. Secondary risk: vllm-ascend's wholesale hf_config_override replacement drops the new dots3_note branch (only matters if Dots3 NOTE were ever enabled on NPU, which is excluded upstream). Tests currently mock the affected parent __init__, so regressions in the new path would not be caught by existing ascend UTs.

commits.message:
[Bugfix] Disable fine-grained prefix-cache hits for incompatible hybrid KV layouts (#51843)

Signed-off-by: mgoin <mgoin64@gmail.com>

affected_interfaces: AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator.__init__ (vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py:160-165) - duplicates the exact `enable_partial_hash_hits` computation this commit fixes in upstream HybridKVCacheCoordinator.__init__
AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator._cache_hit_alignment_tokens (same file:179-183) - alignment granularity (hash_block_size vs scheduler/lcm_block_size) is driven by enable_partial_hash_hits

AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit / find_longest_cache_hit_per_group (same file:266-387, plus base-class per-group lookup used by RecomputeScheduler/DyntraLB/BalanceScheduler) - eagle margin and alignment pass-through depend on enable_partial_hash_hits

Inherited vllm Scheduler.__init__ `mamba_partial_cache_hit` (vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:307) - now gated on `kv_cache_manager.coordinator.enable_partial_hash_hits`; Ascend schedulers (RecomputeScheduler, DyntraLBRecomputeScheduler, SchedulerProfilingChunk, and the patched scheduler in vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py) subclass upstream Scheduler and call `_mamba_block_aligned_split` which reads `mamba_partial_cache_hit`
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: Port the upstream fix into the Ascend duplicate of the modified logic. In `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py` `AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator.__init__`, replace the current `enable_partial_hash_hits` computation (lines 160-165) with the new upstream logic: keep `dcp_world_size == 1 and any(MambaSpec align group with block_size > hash_block_size)` as `has_partial_mamba_group`, then guard it with the new compatibility check that iterates `self.single_type_managers` and disables partial hash hits (plus a `logger.warning_once`) when any manager has `not manager.supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup and manager.block_size != hash_block_size`. Add `from vllm.logger import init_logger` / `logger = init_logger(__name__)` to that patch file (it currently has no logger). Note `manager.block_size` already accounts for dcp scaling but the check only runs at dcp_world_size == 1, matching upstream semantics. No change is needed to the Ascend schedulers themselves since they inherit the upstream `Scheduler.__init__` and the upstream class attribute `enable_partial_hash_hits = False` on the base KVCacheCoordinator avoids any AttributeError for the delegated (non-hybrid) coordinators; the fix only takes effect once the Ascend hybrid coordinator exposes the corrected flag. Add a regression test mirroring upstream `test_hybrid_sliding_window_group_disables_partial_hash_hits` (full + mamba 'align' + SlidingWindowSpec eagle group) asserting `coordinator.enable_partial_hash_hits` is False, e.g. in `tests/ut/test_compressed_prefix_cache.py`.
deep_analysis.risk: Without porting, the correctness bug #51843 fixes persists on the Ascend hybrid path: for a hybrid layout combining a Mamba 'align' group (block_size > hash_block_size) with a non-fine-grained manager whose block_size != hash_block_size (e.g. a SlidingWindowManager eagle group), AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator would still enable fine-grained partial hash hits and the inherited scheduler would keep `mamba_partial_cache_hit=True`, yielding inconsistent per-group hit granularities (fine hash-block-aligned hits from mamba vs block-aligned only from SWA) and incorrect partial-tail CoW/hit registration for models such as DeepSeek-V4 + MTP/EAGLE. This is a silent correctness/performance regression, not a crash. The port itself is low-risk and mechanical; only care needed is verifying the `manager.block_size != hash_block_size` comparison against Ascend effective block sizes (compress_ratio / scheduler_block_size may be None) and confirming `logger.warning_once` is used to avoid log spam.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This commit refactors MRV2 GPUModelRunner so that pre-dispatch CPU request state is gathered in a new `gather_batch_req_state()` (returns a new `BatchReqState` NamedTuple), `prepare_inputs` now takes `(scheduler_output, batch_req_state, batch_desc)`, a new required `has_prefill` field is added to `InputBatch`, and uniform-decode dispatch is gated on `get_uniform_decode_token_count(..., has_prefill)` (all requests must be decoding; a prompt chunk with decode-like shape must NOT be classified as uniform decode). vllm-ascend's MRV2 path breaks at runtime and must be adapted:

1. **vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py `NPUModelRunner.prepare_inputs` (line 284)**: base `GPUModelRunner.execute_model` now calls `self.prepare_inputs(scheduler_output, batch_req_state, batch_desc)` with 3 positional args, so the Ascend override's 2-arg signature `(self, scheduler_output, batch_desc)` raises `TypeError`. Change the signature to `(self, scheduler_output, batch_req_state: BatchReqState, batch_desc: BatchExecutionDescriptor)` and consume the pre-gathered state: use `batch_req_state.req_ids`, `.num_scheduled_tokens`, `.idx_mapping_np`, `.prefill_len_np`, `.num_computed_prefill_tokens_np`, `.is_prefilling_np`, and `.has_prefill` (instead of recomputing from `self.req_states`); feed `has_prefill` into `self.eplb.set_batch_phase(...)`.

2. **AscendInputBatch construction (model_runner.py lines 450-485)**: the base `InputBatch` dataclass gains a non-default `has_prefill: bool` field. The manual `AscendInputBatch(...)` construction omits it and will raise `TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument`. Add `has_prefill=batch_req_state.has_prefill` (i.e. `bool(np.any(is_prefilling_np))`). This field is also read downstream by the base speculators for uniform-decode FULL-graph dispatch.

3. **`_pad_query_start_loc_for_fia` (model_runner.py:558-594)**: its FULL-mode "uniform-batch case" (`num_tokens_padded == num_reqs_padded * self.decode_query_len`) is shape-only and exhibits exactly the bug this commit fixes - a prefill chunk of `decode_query_len` tokens can have a decode batch's shape and must not take the uniform-decode path. Make this branch prefill-aware (e.g. bail to the mixed-batch branch when `batch_req_state.has_prefill` is true) so it stays consistent with `get_uniform_decode_token_count` returning None for prefill batches.

4. **Spec decode paths**: `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py`, `.../eagle/...`, `.../dflash/...` call into base `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.generate_draft_tokens` / `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`, which now pass `input_batch.has_prefill` into `get_uniform_decode_token_count`. Verify Ascend input batches always carry the correct `has_prefill` (from step 2) so FULL ACL-graph uniform-decode replay is never selected for a batch that contains a true prefill. The `flashcomm_dispatch_wrapper` (model_runner.py:86) monkey-patch of `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp` needs no change (it forwards `uniform_token_count`, which is now None for prefills).

5. **PCP path**: base `PCPManager._construct_local_batch` (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pcp_manager.py) now passes `has_prefill=...` via `dataclasses.replace`, which preserves the `AscendInputBatch` type - validate `AscendPCPManager.partition_batch` (pcp_manager.py:62) still receives a well-formed batch and that `seq_lens_np`/`attn_state` refresh uses the new field correctly.

6. **utils.py patch safety**: the existing `patch_bind_kv_cache.py` monkey-patches `vllm.v1.worker.utils.bind_kv_cache`; this commit only *adds* `is_uniform_query_len`/`get_uniform_decode_token_count` to that module, so the patch is unaffected.
deep_analysis.risk: high. The MRV2 path on Ascend breaks outright at runtime with two TypeErrors (prepare_inputs signature mismatch; missing `has_prefill` in the AscendInputBatch dataclass construction), so any MRV2/spec-decode deployment fails until adapted. Beyond the hard breakage, the semantic fix is correctness-relevant on Ascend: the existing `_pad_query_start_loc_for_fia` FULL-mode uniform-batch branch is shape-only and can mis-dispatch a prefill chunk of decode_query_len tokens as a uniform decode ACL graph, producing wrong attention/correctness; that path must be made prefill-aware in lockstep with the new `has_prefill`-gated dispatch to avoid silent incorrect results rather than a clean error.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: No signature/API removals; the change is internal. The promotion logic in vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils._promote_local_kv_cache_specs now rebuilds promoted specs through the new vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface.replace_as helper, which copies ALL init fields (previously only a subset) and dispatches via type(spec).__mro__. Concretely for vllm-ascend: (1) Verify AscendSlinkingWindowMLASpec stays field-compatible with the promotion target MLAAttentionSpec - it currently is (its fields are a re-declaration of upstream SlidingWindowMLASpec fields, all present on MLAAttentionSpec), so no TypeError today, but do NOT add Ascend-only init fields (scale_dim, store_on_host, cache_sparse_sfa_c8, etc.) to any class that can be promoted, or the class-changing replace_as will raise 'unexpected keyword argument'. (2) Note the behavior delta: promoted specs now preserve sliding_window, kv_quant_mode, indexes_kv_by_block_stride and head_size_v that were previously reset to defaults. For DeepSeekV4/AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec this only triggers when --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager is set (unify_hybrid_kv_cache_specs) or via the full-allocation fallback (which excludes SlidingWindowMLASpec, so DeepSeekV4 is unaffected there). (3) Run a DeepSeekV4 regression with --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager and a hybrid SWA/ChunkedLocal model on NPU to confirm KV-cache page sizing and grouping/merge assertions (e.g., FullAttentionSpec.merge sliding_window/attention_chunk_size mutual-exclusion) still hold now that sliding_window is carried onto promoted MLAAttentionSpecs. (4) Track the surrounding [KV-Cache Layout Refactor] series (this is commit 4/N); subsequent commits may further change kv_cache_interface that vllm-ascend subclasses.
deep_analysis.risk: Low-medium. No current runtime breakage: Ascend spec subclasses are field-compatible with the replace_as targets and no interface is removed. Two latent concerns: (a) replace_as copies every init field, so any future Ascend-specific field on a promotable spec subclass (e.g., if AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec grows an NPU layout field) will raise TypeError at engine startup instead of silently dropping the field; (b) preserving sliding_window/kv_quant_mode/indexes_kv_by_block_stride on promoted specs slightly changes KV-cache allocation and merge/grouping behavior in the disabled-hybrid-manager path, which vllm-ascend's DeepSeekV4 grouped path and NPU model runners consume - should be verified, not assumed.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
Mirror the upstream generalization in vllm-ascend's KV block zeroers, which were designed around the old FullAttentionSpec-only zeroing contract:

1. vllm_ascend/worker/utils.py (AscendKVBlockZeroer.init_meta, line ~96): change the guard `if not isinstance(spec, FullAttentionSpec): continue` to `if not isinstance(spec, AttentionSpec): continue` (update the import from `vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface` from FullAttentionSpec to AttentionSpec), so SlidingWindowSpec/ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec groups (incl. AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec used by DeepSeek V4) get registered like in upstream. The block-first layout (block_dim=0, K/V tuple segments) already matches Ascend's `get_kv_cache_shape`.

2. vllm_ascend/_310p/kv_block_zeroer.py (AscendKVBlockZeroer310.init_meta, line ~52): apply the same `isinstance(spec, AttentionSpec)` generalization and import change.

3. Verify the per-group `kernel_block_sizes[group.kv_cache_group_id][0]` entries in model_runner_v1.py (~line 4499-4525) are populated for sliding-window/chunked-local groups (the zeroer indexes by kv_cache_group_id; a missing/0 entry would assert or mis-zero).

4. Handle page-size variance: AscendKVBlockZeroer.init_meta asserts all segments share one uniform `page_size_el` (`assert page_size_el == cur_page_el`), which is fine when only FullAttentionSpec groups registered. With SWA/chunked-local groups added, page sizes may differ across groups; either generalize the kernel to per-segment page sizes (as upstream's `_zero_kv_blocks_kernel` does with seg_page_sizes) or restrict segment collection so recorded IDs always map to registered segments.

5. Add regression tests mirroring upstream tests/v1/worker/test_kv_block_zeroer.py (SlidingWindowSpec/ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec zeroing) and test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py (records_new_block_ids) in tests/ut/ (e.g. extend tests/ut/_310p/test_kv_block_zeroer_310p.py and the worker/coordinator UTs).

6. Check the MRV1 scheduler paths (recompute_scheduler.py:805, dyntra_lb_scheduler.py:995, patch_balance_schedule.py:785) that consume `take_new_block_ids()` / `get_zeroing_block_ids_in_range()`: they now receive IDs from SWA/chunked-local groups too; ensure the zeroer actually covers those groups (otherwise block IDs are drained and silently not zeroed, or — worse — written into full-attention segments at the wrong global block offset, corrupting KV data).
deep_analysis.risk: High if unadapted. With `needs_kv_cache_zeroing=True` (has_mamba_layers or mixed-precision KV cache, e.g. DeepSeek V4 hybrid with Mamba/linear-attention layers) on the MRV1 path, AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec/SlidingWindowSpec/ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec managers now emit new_block_ids_to_zero while AscendKVBlockZeroer/AscendKVBlockZeroer310 register only FullAttentionSpec segments. Because block IDs come from a single shared BlockPool, zeroing a SWA-allocated block ID writes zeros into the full-attention cache at an arbitrary offset (memory corruption / accuracy degradation), or the blocks are silently left stale/unzeroed. The adaptation itself is small in code but touches segment-address bookkeeping and per-segment page-size assumptions, so careful testing on DeepSeek V4 + Eagle3/MTP is required.
